nodes.rationale: The observed leader uses a 1-ATR stop, 2.5 reward multiple and thirty-minute maximum hold, earning $15.45 from three same-day FTFT trades. It is a validation candidate within the existing 27-policy grid, not an approved replacement or independent validation result.

nodes.label: Chronological selection and untouched holdout
nodes.rationale: Register universe, dates, constraints and precision before inspecting outcomes; account for parameter search and cost/delay sensitivity, freeze a candidate only after development criteria pass, then evaluate once on a later untouched holdout. Insufficient evidence or failed validation leaves the selected configuration empty.

nodes.label: Eligibility and fill funnel audit
nodes.rationale: Proposes tracing coverage, eligibility, alerts, plans, orders and fills before calibration to distinguish missing data, strategy filters and execution assumptions. Expiry alone does not show a parameter is wrong; entry changes alter the trades entering the portfolio and require exit revalidation.

nodes.label: SES and TE admission rejections
nodes.rationale: SES's 26 alerts and TE's 28 alerts yielded no orders because of reward/risk, empty price intervals, stale quotes and session-time restrictions. Separate accounts eliminate cash competition but cannot eliminate admission failures. Their zero account P&L is distinct from an unavailable trade-return estimate.

nodes.label: Current simulated research scope
nodes.rationale: Records $10,000 starting cash per alternative cash account, qualifying signals, all-affordable requests subject to modeled capacity, approximately fifteen-minute intraday exits, and removal of the $100 account-drawdown control. Earlier capital settings and longer holding explorations remain historical rather than cumulative account results.

nodes.label: Timer-only holding horizons
nodes.rationale: With price exits disabled, two minutes earns $35.754, fifteen minutes loses $63.726, sixty minutes loses $105.016, and close minus sixty seconds earns $642.964 nominally. The near-close outcome requires almost six hours and seven future quote-linked fills; longer holding is not consistently better.

nodes.label: FTFT SES TE GRAB RR SERV alternative-account cohort
nodes.norm_label: ftft ses te grab rr serv alternative-account cohort
nodes.rationale: Each symbol/rule combination has continuous settled cash and one filled episode per day. The other five stocks submit no orders; 48 of their 88 alerts have empty price intervals. Exit changes cannot repair entry feasibility, and original >=1.5 reward/risk admission does not promise the modified exits' payoff.

nodes.label: Consolidated research findings and questions
nodes.rationale: Synthesizes eleven historical reports without running new experiments; separates improved simulator engineering from the still-unestablished predictive trading edge.

nodes.label: Stage 1 consolidated research synthesis
nodes.rationale: Contains the same consolidated findings and discussion as research_findings_and_questions.md, including the eleven-report coverage table and the distinction between engineering verification and economic validation.

nodes.label: Cross-stock fifteen-minute qualifying-entry study
nodes.rationale: Runs FTFT, SES and TE in separate $1,000 alternative cash accounts across nine dates while preserving qualifying entries. FTFT supplies one losing trade; SES and TE supply no trades, so the study does not establish traded cross-stock performance.

nodes.label: Holding-period investigation
nodes.rationale: Compares seven holding deadlines with price exits retained or disabled, across three fixtures, on the same known FTFT entry. Forty-two counterfactual cells remain one underlying opportunity.

nodes.label: Lenient entry comparison with $10,000 cash
nodes.rationale: Reports thirty-six primary alternative accounts, strict-capital controls and repeats. Eleven distinct entries across five stocks produce three positive, twenty-seven negative and six no-trade accounts. The 98 targeted tests and 152 audit groups validate the offline comparison, while nine exposed dates, prior outcome selection and missing data leave trading acceptance unsupported.

nodes.label: Lenient $10,000 simulation summary
nodes.rationale: Condenses the full lenient-entry study: six stocks and six exits, wider caps, admission reduced to 1.0, and ten additional losing opportunities. Explicitly treats cells as alternative accounts and engineering checks as distinct from profitability evidence; it is not another experiment.

nodes.label: Six exit rules across six stocks
nodes.norm_label: six exit rules across six stocks
nodes.rationale: Runs thirty-six alternative $1,000 accounts over nine dates. Only FTFT trades, so adding SES, TE, GRAB, RR and SERV does not expand executed opportunities. All six exits profit on the same previously exposed FTFT entry.

nodes.label: Registered research priorities and unresolved requirements
nodes.norm_label: registered research priorities and unresolved requirements
nodes.rationale: Proposes choosing an after-cost success measure, specifying broker and order behavior, acquiring fresh prespecified evidence, diagnosing accepted and rejected entries, and evaluating shared-account selection before further tuning. Broker, data budget, stock-universe constraints, and entry redesign remain discussion questions.

nodes.label: Fifteen-minute exit-request deadline
nodes.rationale: The primary timer disables original price exits and requests liquidation 900 seconds after the actual fill. Nominal completion took 901.349644012 seconds and lost $63.726, with routing and future capacity governing completion. Original reward/risk remains only an admission filter, and unresolved close-of-session exposure would stop the branch rather than create a sale.

nodes.label: Exposed pre-close analysis and incomplete adverse marks
nodes.norm_label: exposed pre-close analysis and incomplete adverse marks
nodes.rationale: The pre-close horizon was included after later marks were inspected, so freezing executions did not make the study independent validation. Worst pre-request marks neither model full liquidation nor measure peak-to-trough account drawdown; an approximately 300-second archived quote gap leaves unobserved losses unknown. Overnight carry was not modeled.

nodes.label: Retained-stop precedence over longer deadlines
nodes.rationale: The original stop requested sale at 727.588547403 seconds, before the fifteen-minute maximum. Extending the deadline to thirty minutes, sixty minutes or pre-close therefore preserves exactly the same stop execution and loss; a longer maximum does not disable earlier triggers.

nodes.label: Coverage-based universe selection amendment
nodes.rationale: A retrospective assets screen yielded 1,024 candidates, 164 daily-filter passes and twelve minute preflights. Full pre-period coverage selected only GRAB, so the preserved failed criterion was amended before test acquisition to require 21 consecutive opening minutes and rank coverage and liquidity. GRAB, SERV and RR were selected; the six-stock panel still has 934 missing regular-session minute slots.

nodes.label: breakeven_1atr exit policy
nodes.community_name: All-in cash-account simulation and exit comparison
nodes.rationale: After one ATR of net marked gain, raises the stop to cost-aware breakeven rounded upward. The nominal stop became $4.96, but delayed, partial execution below that trigger still lost $5.006.

nodes.label: fixed_15m exit policy
nodes.community_name: All-in cash-account simulation and exit comparison
nodes.rationale: Retains the 1.5-ATR initial stop, 2R target and fifteen-minute deadline. The nominal 199-share trade lost $76.906 as capacity-limited liquidation sold successive shares below the stop trigger.

nodes.label: trail_1atr exit policy
nodes.community_name: All-in cash-account simulation and exit comparison
nodes.rationale: After one ATR of net marked gain, raises the stop monotonically to the greater of breakeven and highest observed bid minus one frozen ATR. Its higher final stop triggered slightly earlier, but routing reached the same executable quotes as breakeven, producing the same $5.006 nominal loss.

nodes.label: All-in cash-account simulation and exit comparison
nodes.community_name: All-in cash-account simulation and exit comparison
nodes.norm_label: all-in cash-account simulation and exit comparison
nodes.rationale: Implements all-affordable cash sizing and removes the $100 account-drawdown control. Ten registered executions compare three exits across nominal, doubled-cost and doubled-delay fixtures on the same FTFT entry; protective exits reduce loss without establishing profitability.

nodes.label: All-affordable settled-cash sizing
nodes.community_name: All-in cash-account simulation and exit comparison
nodes.rationale: Requested quantity is floor(available_settled_cash / (entry_cap + entry_fee_per_share)). The old planning cap and financial sizing ceilings are removed, while future quote capacity, IOC cancellation, one filled episode per date and settlement remain. The nominal 199-share entry spent $985.448; larger exits encountered later, worse-priced capacity, so losses do not scale linearly from fifty shares.

nodes.community_name: Historical replay pilot and account-model updates
nodes.rationale: Uses FTFT, SES and TE over four September sessions with a 1.5-ATR stop, 2R target, fifteen-minute hold, and engineering assumptions for costs and latency. Four FTFT trades lost $23.60; 424 tests, deterministic repetition and 26 artifact checks establish offline implementation behavior rather than profitability.

nodes.label: Momentum score 85 and entry extension
nodes.community_name: Historical replay pilot and account-model updates
nodes.rationale: The confirmed score of 85 followed a 30.32% five-minute rise and 20.50% extension above VWAP. RSI 76.31 removed points rather than vetoing entry. The score is a weighted checklist, not an 85% success probability; the last prefill score remained eligible at 90, so stale-signal failure was not established.

nodes.label: Fifty-share planning liquidity cap
nodes.community_name: Historical replay pilot and account-model updates
nodes.rationale: Maximum-allocation variant C still bought 50 FTFT shares because 25% of the observed 200-share planning bid size bound quantity below cash capacity 199 and risk capacity 242. The $247.60 deployment and identical B/C outcomes identify the binding model constraint without establishing actual market capacity.

nodes.label: Cash-account loss diagnosis
nodes.community_name: Historical replay pilot and account-model updates
nodes.rationale: Diagnoses one frozen FTFT opportunity, its signal, target geometry, admission funnel, selection rule and execution costs without a new strategy replay or parameter search.

nodes.label: Historical replay pilot and account-model updates
nodes.community_name: Historical replay pilot and account-model updates
nodes.norm_label: historical replay pilot and account-model updates
nodes.rationale: Preserves successive experiments: the original $10,000 pilot lost $23.60, the $1,000 guarded baseline lost $11.30, and settled-cash variants A and B/C lost $11.026 and $18.70 respectively. These are separate models and account configurations, not cumulative P&L.

nodes.label: Alpaca order documentation
nodes.community_name: Historical replay pilot and account-model updates
nodes.rationale: The report cites two-decimal limit-price precision at or above $1 and four decimals below $1 as broker-specific order-entry documentation, explicitly not a universal data tick rule or confirmation of the intended broker.

nodes.label: Proposed simulation improvements and research priorities
nodes.community_name: Historical replay pilot and account-model updates
nodes.norm_label: proposed simulation improvements and research priorities
nodes.rationale: Proposes execution-contract verification and causal diagnostics before broader entry/exit experiments. Its $1,000 capital and $100 drawdown requirements describe the historical baseline, and no new implementation or backtests are claimed.

nodes.label: Prospective recording and clock uncertainty
nodes.community_name: Historical replay pilot and account-model updates
nodes.rationale: Twenty newly acquired sessions were minute-only, and the 180.018-second prospective capture retained 743 records. With unmeasured local clock accuracy and 382 negative receipt-minus-provider timestamp differences among 718 quote/trade observations, the capture cannot calibrate execution latency or supply an execution-ready holdout.

nodes.label: Running-peak drawdown guard and unknown equity
nodes.community_name: Historical replay pilot and account-model updates
nodes.norm_label: running-peak drawdown guard and unknown equity
nodes.rationale: The historical $1,000 account uses a fixed $100 threshold below the running equity peak. Unknown valuation blocks new risk, and threshold detection cancels entries and routes exits; gaps, latency and capacity can still overshoot. The baseline observed $43 drawdown and 40.915 seconds of unknown equity, so observed marks do not certify a continuous maximum loss.

nodes.label: Empty admissible entry-price interval
nodes.community_name: Historical replay pilot and account-model updates
nodes.rationale: Twenty-seven of 71 alerts were structurally rejected when one-cent rounding and a 0.25-ATR chase allowance made cap equal trigger despite positive displacement. All had ATR below $0.04. The example requires ask >= $4.49 and ask <= $4.489; rejecting it is correct, while price-grid compatibility remains a research assumption. Funnel blockers overlap and do not imply rejected opportunities would profit.

nodes.label: Settled cash and T+1 funding model
nodes.community_name: Historical replay pilot and account-model updates
nodes.norm_label: settled cash and t+1 funding model
nodes.rationale: Separates settled cash, reservations and signed unsettled proceeds. Sales remain in equity but cannot finance another intraday round trip; calendar-based availability is modeled at 09:30 Eastern on T+1. Structural infeasibility is rejected before reservation. Settlement transfers do not create profits, and actual broker posting time is unknown.

nodes.label: Causal order diagnostics and execution-state timing
nodes.community_name: Historical replay pilot and account-model updates
nodes.norm_label: causal order diagnostics and execution-state timing
nodes.rationale: Proposes separate event, receipt, decision, submission, activation, fill-report and cancellation-acknowledgment times. Strategy knowledge can differ from actual simulated holdings. Quote marks must be distinguished from capacity-constrained liquidation; isolated delay sensitivities, partial-fill replenishment and fill/cancel races need explicit treatment.

nodes.label: Registered evidence expansion and controlled hypotheses
nodes.community_name: Historical replay pilot and account-model updates
nodes.norm_label: registered evidence expansion and controlled hypotheses
nodes.rationale: Requires prespecified historical membership, coverage and corporate-action checks, retained exclusions, independent symbol-dates, prospective clock evidence and dependency-aware precision criteria. Entry extension, exit geometry, revalidation and selection are bounded strategy hypotheses to attribute individually before testing a combination on untouched evidence.

nodes.label: Versioned broker price and entry-execution contract
nodes.community_name: Historical replay pilot and account-model updates
nodes.norm_label: versioned broker price and entry-execution contract
nodes.rationale: Twenty-seven impossible entry intervals motivate verifying instrument, order-type and date-specific order precision; locally triggered IOC versus broker-native behavior; and separation of price limits, displacement and fees. A justified model correction requires consistent rules and rejection audits, not improved P&L or forced fills.

nodes.label: Strict capital control and partial-fill scaling
nodes.community_name: Historical replay pilot and account-model updates
nodes.norm_label: strict capital control and partial-fill scaling
nodes.rationale: Strict $1,000 versus strict $10,000 two-minute accounts isolates capital: FTFT requests 1,999 shares but fills 950, deploys $4,704.40 and earns $185.950, versus 199 shares and $35.754. Account return falls despite higher dollar profit. Strict versus lenient $10,000 combines cap widening and reward/risk relaxation and cannot attribute them separately.

nodes.label: Lenient entry-cap and reward-risk geometry
nodes.community_name: Historical replay pilot and account-model updates
nodes.rationale: Changes starting cash to $10,000, cap to the larger of the old cap and trigger plus displacement plus $0.01 rounded upward, and minimum original-geometry net reward/risk from 1.5 to 1.0. Nominal displacement makes minimum cap two cents above trigger, allowing $0.019 of ask movement. Dependent quantity, reservation and target-at-cap values are recomputed; original stop, ATR, signals and freshness gates remain.

nodes.label: Avellaneda–Stoikov reservation-price interpretation
nodes.rationale: The displayed algebra matches the reservation-price formula conventionally interpreting s as mid-price, q as inventory, γ as risk aversion, σ as volatility, and T − t as remaining time. The image supplies no symbol definitions or model attribution, so these meanings are inferred.

nodes.label: Conditional linear shift from the baseline
nodes.norm_label: conditional linear shift from the baseline
nodes.rationale: Holding the other parameters fixed, r changes linearly with q. If γσ²(T − t) is positive, positive q places r below s and negative q places r above s. The formula alone does not establish parameter signs or units.

nodes.label: FTFT September 14 breakout reversal
nodes.rationale: Fifty shares entered at $4.951 and exited at $4.579 after the $4.59 stop, losing $18.70. No holding-period quote reached the $5.68 target; the $5.23 high was a conditional mark with limited displayed capacity. Price movement dominated the loss, while delayed execution and costs further reduced proceeds.

nodes.label: Eight earlier-exit counterfactuals
nodes.rationale: Compares 0.5/1-ATR profit targets, breakeven after 0.5 ATR, 0.5/0.25-ATR trails, a tighter initial stop, unconditional 120-second exit and a one-time conditional progress check. Nominal one-ATR target earns $51.194 and unconditional two-minute exit $35.754; tighter initial stop still loses, while the positive-progress check permits the original later loss.

nodes.label: SERV profitable trigger with losing fills
nodes.norm_label: serv profitable trigger with losing fills
nodes.rationale: A September 14 observation at $4.42 triggered a target or protective stop, yet 625 shares sold at $4.409 after a $4.411 entry and lost $2.50 including fees. Matching protection outcomes do not imply protection never activated. The stored highest_observed_bid omits a terminal target-trigger quote and is not a complete post-entry maximum.

nodes.label: FINRA order-types guide
nodes.rationale: Cited for the price versus non-execution tradeoff of limit orders, without establishing the experiment's numerical parameters.

nodes.label: Earlier profit-taking investigation
nodes.rationale: Tests eight frozen exit-only rules after the original FTFT path was already known, preserving the original 199-share entry and scenario-specific fills. Six rules profit in three fixtures, but this outcome-informed diagnostic does not establish an optimal or accepted trading policy.

nodes.label: SEC stop-order bulletin
nodes.rationale: Cited for execution-price limitations of stop orders, not to calibrate the study's ATR or timing constants.

nodes.label: ATR payoff geometry versus hit probability
nodes.norm_label: atr payoff geometry versus hit probability
nodes.rationale: ATR $0.23465 and the rounded 1.5-ATR stop produced about 7.29% downside and a 2R target requiring about 14.72% upside within fifteen minutes. These equations define price distances, not probabilities or arrival times, so nominal reward/risk alone cannot establish positive expected profit.

nodes.label: Cost-adjusted exit formulas
nodes.rationale: For entry e, frozen ATR A, entry/exit fees a/b and exit displacement g: breakeven = round_up(e+a+b+g); profit_trigger(beta) = min(original_target, round_up(e+a+b+g+beta*A)); net_marked_gain = max(0,observed_bid-g)-b-e-a. Earlier protection arms at 0.5 ATR; trailing stops never decrease and ATR never refreshes.

nodes.label: Early-exit payoff and admission mismatch
nodes.rationale: Ideal small-target rewards of $0.126/$0.236 against $0.364 loss imply reward/risk about 0.346/0.648 and simplified break-even winner fractions 74.3%/60.7%. These are not observed success rates. Original >=1.5 admission was not rerun for the fixed-entry diagnostic, so full-strategy integration must revisit actual payoff admission.

nodes.label: Profit triggers versus executed proceeds
nodes.rationale: The $5.08 crossing reversed within roughly four milliseconds and produced a $4.999 fill after delays. A conditional peak mark covered only 25 shares of a 199-share position. All target rules request delayed market liquidation; resting limits would need a separate queue and non-fill model, because touching a price is not a sale.

nodes.label: Eleven entries and ten added losing opportunities
nodes.community_name: Entry quality as the next research priority
nodes.norm_label: eleven entries and ten added losing opportunities
nodes.rationale: The 66 primary trade records repeat eleven stock/time opportunities across six exits. Every added opportunity loses under every exit; SES never reaches protection, TE and GRAB hit original stops under the five longer policies, and RR's four orders expire. Increased participation did not improve profitability on the tested dates.

nodes.label: Entry quality as the next research priority
nodes.community_name: Entry quality as the next research priority
nodes.norm_label: entry quality as the next research priority
nodes.rationale: The momentum score is uncalibrated, repeated exit comparisons reuse one known FTFT opportunity, and all ten entries added by leniency lost under every tested exit. The report prioritizes entry discrimination, fresh evaluation data, and a defensible execution contract without selecting a profitable replacement.

nodes.label: Unresolved selection for one shared account
nodes.community_name: Entry quality as the next research priority
nodes.norm_label: unresolved selection for one shared account
nodes.rationale: Separate stock/rule accounts do not establish how one account should rank simultaneous opportunities, wait, or remain flat. The proposed evaluation must use contemporaneous information, shared settled cash, prespecified success criteria, and separately attributed entry changes.

nodes.label: First feasible confirmed-alert selection
nodes.community_name: Entry quality as the next research priority
nodes.rationale: The single-entry rule chooses the first feasible alert chronologically with alphabetical ties, rather than estimating expected return. It blocked 21 later alerts despite $752.40 of unused settled cash. Two later trades improved variant A by $7.674 on this day, but one-day evidence does not establish a superior selection policy.
